memoryNote: Learner lives near Tokyo and works in IT. Has a five-year-old son. Wakes up at 5:30 and studies English before work. Likes ramen, sci-fi movies and Fukuoka. Needs English for company meetings; understands more than he can say.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: I tried to make bread last weekend and it came out flat like a pancake.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Flat bread! That is still bread, kind of.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: What about you, did anything go wrong for you recently?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Yes. I try to cook curry but I forget the rice.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Curry with no rice is a soup, right?

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: So what did you eat it with in the end?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Bread.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Bread and curry, that is actually a real combination in some places.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Tell me more about how the curry tasted.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: It was too spicy because I put many chili. My mouth was on fire and I drink milk.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Milk is the correct emergency button, I use it too.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: How spicy do you usually like your food?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Not so spicy. I am weak person for spicy food.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Same here, I am a level one player.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: What is one dish you can cook without any trouble?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Maybe omelette. I make it every morning for my son, he is five years old.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: I am definitely a night person, my brain wakes up at eleven pm.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Are you a morning person or a night person?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I am morning person. I wake up at five thirty every day.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Five thirty is early. What do you do in that quiet time?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I read book and drink coffee. Sometime I study English too.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Studying before the world wakes up, that is a power move.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: How long have you kept this routine?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: About two years. Before that I was night person but I change after my son born.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Kids rewrite the whole schedule, I hear.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: What was the hardest part about changing?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Hello.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: The first weeks are usually the hardest, so what helped you get through them?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I go to bed early, before ten. But weekend is difficult, I want to watch movie.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Weekends are where good habits go to nap.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: What kind of movies do you stay up for?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: えっと、SF movie. Star Wars とか、そういうの。I like space story.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Space stories are worth losing sleep over, I will allow it.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Which one would you recommend to someone who has never watched them?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Maybe Interstellar. It is little difficult but very beautiful.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Adding it to my list right now.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: What made it beautiful for you?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Hmm, it is getting late. Maybe I should think about dinner soon.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: If I could move anywhere, I would pick a small town near the sea.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: I would pick somewhere with a big bookstore.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: If you could move anywhere, where would you go?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I want to live in Fukuoka. I go there last year and the food was amazing.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Fukuoka ramen is dangerous, you cannot stop at one bowl.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: What did you eat there that you still think about?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Motsunabe. It is hot pot with beef. Very rich taste.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Rich and warm, that sounds like a winter dish.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Would you move for the food alone?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Ha ha, maybe fifty percent food. Also the city is not too big, and rent is cheap than Tokyo.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: What would you miss most about where you live now?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: My friends. And my mansion is very convenient, near the station.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: A mansion near the station, you are living the dream.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: How far is the station from your place?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Five minutes walking. Very good for rainy day.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: That is close. What would make you finally decide to move?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Maybe if my company allow remote work forever. By the way, how do you say 引っ越し in English?

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: We say "moving" or "moving house", for example "I am moving next month". So would remote work be enough to push you?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I think yes. But my wife want to stay near her parents, so it is difficult.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Family gravity is strong.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Have you two talked about a compromise?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Not seriously yet. Someday we discuss it.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Someday is a very safe word.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: What would you want the conversation to start with?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: This was fun. I have to go now. Goodbye, see you!

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Today's word is "put off". It means to delay something to a later time.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Oh, I put off my homework every single week.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Can you try making a sentence with it?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I put off my dentist appointment.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Brave. The dentist always wins in the end.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Nice. Why did you put it off?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Because I am scared. Also I was busy in work last month.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: That is a natural use. Can you use it about something at work?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I put off the meeting to next week because my boss was sick.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Sick boss, free week, not bad.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Good. Now try it in past tense with a longer sentence.

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Last year I put off my English study for many months, and I regret it.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: That is a strong sentence. What made you start again?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: My company decide to use English in meeting. So I have no choice.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Nothing motivates like having no escape.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: How do you feel about those meetings now?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: Still nervous but better. I can understand almost, but speaking is difficult.

messages.speaker: chobi
messages.text: Can you make one more sentence with "put off", about the future this time?

messages.speaker: user
messages.text: I will not put off my presentation preparation this time.

messages.speaker: naruko
messages.text: Write that down and put it on the wall.
